en virkelighed.explanation: "En virkelighed" means "a reality". A very common phrase is "i virkeligheden" (in reality): "I virkeligheden er han meget genert" (In reality, he is very shy).

en virkning.explanation: "En virkning" means "an effect". With "bi-" (by) in front, it is "en bivirkning" (a side effect). To say a medicine has a side effect: "Medicinen har en bivirkning" (The medicine has a side effect).

en virksomhed.explanation: "En virksomhed" means "a business". A common word partner is "privat" (private): "en privat virksomhed" (a private business).

en virus.explanation: "En virus" means "a virus". To say you are sick because of one, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en virus" (I have a virus).

en vision.explanation: "En vision" means "a vision", as in a plan for the future. To talk about eyesight, use "et syn" (eyesight): "Jeg har dårligt syn" (My eyesight is bad).

en vissen blomst.explanation: "En vissen blomst" means "a withered flower". It comes from the verb "at visne" (to wither). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "vissen": "et vissent blad" (a withered leaf).

en vitamin.explanation: "En vitamin" means "a vitamin". To name a vitamin, put the letter first: "C-vitamin" (vitamin C).

en vits.explanation: "En vits" means "a joke". The last line that makes people laugh is "en pointe" (a punchline). To say you did not get the joke: "Jeg forstod ikke pointen" (I did not get the point).

en vittighed.explanation: "En vittighed" means "a joke". It is built from "vittig" (witty) and the ending "-hed". To say someone tells a joke: "Han fortæller en vittighed" (He tells a joke).

en vogn.explanation: "En vogn" means "a wagon / cart". As the last part of a word, "vogn" is in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart): "Jeg skubber indkøbsvognen" (I push the shopping cart).

en vokal.explanation: "En vokal" means "a vowel". Danish has nine vowel letters: "a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y", "æ", "ø" and "å".

en voksen.explanation: "En voksen" means "an adult". The word comes from "at vokse" (to grow). To say a film is for adults, use "for voksne": "en film for voksne" (a film for adults).

en vorte.explanation: "En vorte" means "a wart". To say a doctor takes it off: "Lægen fjerner vorten" (The doctor removes the wart).

en vugge.explanation: "En vugge" means "a cradle". The matching verb is "at vugge" (to rock). To say you rock a baby: "Hun vugger barnet" (She rocks the baby).

en vuggestue.explanation: "En vuggestue" means "a nursery". It is built from "en vugge" (a cradle) and "en stue" (a room). In Denmark, children go there until about three years old, then to "en børnehave" (a kindergarten): "Hun går i børnehave" (She goes to kindergarten).

en vulkan.explanation: "En vulkan" means "a volcano". To talk about an eruption, use "et vulkanudbrud" (a volcanic eruption): "Der var et vulkanudbrud på Island" (There was a volcanic eruption in Iceland).

en vurdering.explanation: "En vurdering" means "an assessment". It comes from the verb "at vurdere" (to assess). To give an estimate of what something is worth: "Vurderingen af huset er to millioner kroner" (The assessment of the house is two million kroner).

en våbenhvile.explanation: "En våbenhvile" means "a ceasefire". It is built from "et våben" (a weapon) and "en hvile" (a rest).

en vædder.explanation: "En vædder" means "a ram". The star sign Aries is "Væderen" (the Ram): "Væderen er et stjernetegn" (Aries is a star sign).

en væg.explanation: "En væg" means "a wall", as in inside a room. For a wall outdoors, such as around a garden, use "en mur" (a wall of brick or stone): "Haven har en høj mur" (The garden has a tall wall).

en vægt.explanation: "En vægt" means "a weight / a scale". To ask how heavy someone is: "Hvad er din vægt?" (What is your weight?) To talk about the machine you stand on to weigh yourself: "Vægten står på badeværelset" (The scale is in the bathroom).

en vælger.explanation: "En vælger" means "a voter". It comes from "at vælge" (to choose). To ask who someone votes for, use "at stemme" (to vote): "Hvem stemmer du på?" (Who are you voting for?)

en værdi.explanation: "En værdi" means "a value". To talk about what a person finds important, use the plural "værdier": "Vores værdier er ærlighed og frihed" (Our values are honesty and freedom).

en vært.explanation: "En vært" means "a host", as in the person who has guests. It also means the host of a show: "Hun er vært på et tv-program" (She is the host of a TV show). The word is part of "et værtshus" (a pub): "Vi mødes på værtshuset" (We meet at the pub).

en værtinde.explanation: "En værtinde" means "a hostess". It is "en vært" (a host) plus the ending "-inde", which marks a woman, as in "en veninde" (a female friend).
